newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JULY 16.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Education Minister and former defence minister Gerasimos Arsenis yesterday indicated his desire to play a leading role for ruling party PASOK's internal dissidents with a letter to Prime Minister Costas Simitis outlining his objections to the signing of an agreement between Greece and Turkey at the Madrid NATO summit last week. The letter comes just a few days before the party's Central Committee convenes and where it is expected a full range of objections to the agreement will be aired.

--The prospect of Cyprus's inclusion in the European Union and the beginning of negotiations in April next year will be confirmed by the European Commission in an opinion expected to be released today. The opinion is expected to state that the course of talks for Cyprus's accession to the EU will not be affected by any developments in talks on a possible settlement of the Cyprus problem.

--'Vultures cawing above a sheep' is how Archbishop of Greece Serapheim characterised his would-be successors yesterday. Serapheim slammed the undeclared war that has broken out over the issue of his successor, once again denying reports that he plans to resign within the month.

--The foodstuffs industry yesterday declared war against supermarkets, saying that consumers were being forced to pay up to 15-20 percent more for their purchases. Supermarkets countered, saying they had the lowest profits and calling for talks with the industry. The government, fearing effects on inflation, says it will regulate the issue with a new bill currently being drafted.
--The government yesterday announced a partial ban on lorries over summer weekends on national roads. The measure is hoped to alleviate traffic congestion and reduce the road toll.
--The development ministry is reportedly ready to step in and mediate in the row between the food industry and supermarkets.
--Internal papers at Athens General Hospital reveal serious negligence in work on the radiology service that may have constituted a health hazard to patients.
--With the last of restrictions on foreign exchange to be lifted by the end of the month, Greeks will be able to open accounts in foreign exchange.
--Alexia Glicksbourg, the eldest daughter of Greece's former king Constantine is reportedly in thrall to a 30-year-old Spanish athlete.
--Major changes are expected in the structure of ministries, prepared by Deputy Public Administration Minister Tassos Mantellis, according to reports. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
